title: Porridge with apple and rhubarb compote

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, fresh fruit, seeds, cinnamon and a spoonful of brown sugar are all plain cupboard and garden foods.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient, including March rhubarb and pumpkin seeds, is on the shelf at Tesco at an everyday price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a frying pan, two saucepans and a grater, and the techniques are simple simmering and toasting.

works.reason: 200g oats to 1.2 litres water gives four proper bowls, and four apples with 200g rhubarb, orange juice and a little sugar makes a well-balanced compote in the stated time.

honest_times.reason: Coring four apples, cutting rhubarb, zesting an orange and toasting seeds fits in about 15 minutes, with the porridge cooking alongside the compote for a 20-minute total.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Early forced rhubarb and stored apples are right for mid-March, and the warm compote is the point of the bowl.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, in British English and easy for a beginner to follow, with no restaurant language.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oats, plenty of fruit and toasted seeds make a filling, real-food breakfast with little added sugar.
